bias_controls: The candidate and control are independent IID Gaussian return series with no injected autocorrelation.
Seeds and thresholds are inherited from a digest-bound preregistration before execution.
Every declared seed is reported; no false positive may be hidden.
The lagged rule, sample size, split, and turnover cost match the positive-control experiments.
failure_modes: Gaussian IID returns are much simpler than real markets.
Thirty-two seeds only bound, rather than eliminate, the false-positive probability.
Rejecting this null does not prove that future real-data discoveries are valid.
The negative control tests one strategy and one cost model only.
hypothesis: On independent IID candidate and control series, the unchanged opportunity rule will produce false positives on at most 10% of seeds and the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound will not exceed 20%.
next_experiment: Define the first real-data due-diligence contract: provider, instrument universe, timestamps, survivorship controls, costs, licenses, and a no-capital exploration budget.
title: Independent IID negative-control rejection gate
